item.title: Gas explosion rocks NNPC station in Lagos, damages school
item.description: By Esther Onyegbula & Olasunkanmi Akoni A gas explosion at a Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) filling station at Savannah Bus Stop, Command, Ejigbo, Lagos State, triggered a fire that spread to an adjoining school, damaging parts of its premises. No casualty was recorded in the incident, which occurred at about 1 p.m., as the school, Saint Lawrence Greater Height School, was closed for the weekend. The Controller-General of the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, Margaret Adeseye, confirmed the incident, saying the prompt intervention of firefighters prevented the fire from spreading to other sections of the school and causing further damage. Adeseye said the agency received a distress call at 12:50 p.m. and arrived at the scene at 1:13 p.m. following reports of an explosion and an ensuing fire at the filling station. She said firefighters from the Ejigbo, Ikeja and Bolade fire stations were immediately deployed to the scene to contain the blaze and prevent it from spreading to neighbouring buildings. According to her, the intensity of the explosion caused the fire to spread rapidly from the filling station to the adjoining school, affecting parts of the institution’s premises. She, however, said the firefighters worked collaboratively to bring the situation under control and prevented the fire from engulfing other sections of the school. “No casualty was recorded in the incident,” Adeseye stated. She added that preliminary investigations had commenced to establish the circumstances surrounding the explosion. The incident has renewed concerns over the safety risks associated with gas-related operations at filling stations, particularly facilities located close to schools and other public institutions. The fire service urged members of the public to remain safety-conscious as investigations into the cause of the explosion continue. Vanguard Newspaper The post Gas explosion rocks NNPC station in Lagos, damages school appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ubuntu gets AI-generated security fixes for those feeling brave
item.description: Canonical is offering Ubuntu Pro users an opt-in channel for AI-generated security patches, deploying bots to help tackle the growing pile of vulnerabilities other bots are uncovering. Canonical's VP for "Excellence Engineering," Pierre Guillemin, gave the second keynote at the recent Ubuntu Summit, introducing the Edge archive , an optional repository of security fixes generated by the company's Surge framework. As the announcement describes it: "We built Surge, a multi-agent orchestration framework for CVE remediation and backporting, and have reached a high level of confidence in its capabilities. We will not automatically upload Surge-generated fixes to our stable releases, but from today they are available to Ubuntu Pro users in the new Edge archive." Edge offers patches before extended testing and qualification are complete, allowing users to assess them themselves. Canonical says updates delivered through the normal security channels will remain human-validated. Ubuntu Summit now runs twice a year. Last week's Ubuntu Summit 26.10 followed a rather unfortunately timed server outage for the company . At the previous such event in June , the company announced a move into agentic AI, but this new one is bolder still. Guillemin noted that "October 2026 saw almost as many CVEs as all of 2025." Surge is a "multi-agent orchestration framework" to remediate vulnerabilities in Ubuntu's userspace. In other words, not the kernel, but even so, it is ambitious. The idea is to use a group of different LLMs to triage new vulnerabilities, find existing fixes, use multiple competing models to backport them to the versions in Ubuntu, and run automatic testing on them. Then a different group of "judging models" will evaluate the fixes and look for consensus. When candidates are chosen, they pass through normal Ubuntu package testing. If there are edge cases, low confidence scores, deadlocks, or other problems, then the process will be escalated to the staff of Canonical's security team. It's an attempt, as Guillemin put it, "to use AI to fight AI" – cooperating groups of LLMs patching their way through the ever-increasing flow of security holes. Even so, this is a remarkably courageous tactic (at the risk of using a famous British euphemism ). It's an opt-in feature of Ubuntu Pro, Canonical's security and support subscription – although as we reported in 2022 , Pro also has a free tier, so security researchers and the community can try Edge out, study it, and report their findings. We do sympathize with companies struggling against a rising tide of bot-powered security hole discovery. In theory, corporate funding can pay for faster fixes than a volunteer community can offer, but even for commercial vendors these are testing times. As we reported when Debian turned 30 , surveys suggest that Ubuntu is about a third of the world Linux user base. item.title: 'Maybe the scariest thing I've heard in my life': Artemis II astronaut Victor Glover reveals his toughest challenge before flying to the moon
item.description: null TENERIFE, Canary Islands — Former NASA astronaut Victor Glover has flown in combat, performed four spacewalks and strapped himself to the top of rockets launching into space. But before embarking on his historic Artemis II journey around the moon, he faced something even more difficult: a conversation with his four daughters. Speaking alongside former astronaut Chris Hadfield at the Starmus VIII festival in Tenerife, Canary Islands, on Oct. 18, Glover opened up about the challenges of preparing his family for his riskiest mission yet. "This is maybe the greatest challenge of my astronaut career," Glover said. Glover joined NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman and Christina Koch and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen aboard NASA's Artemis II mission, which launched on April 1 , 2026, marking humanity's first crewed journey to the moon since Apollo 17 in 1972. But preparing for the historic journey wasn't just about mastering the spacecraft and executing the mission successfully. It also meant making sure his family was ready for what lay ahead. When Glover first traveled to space aboard SpaceX's Crew-1 mission in 2020, his children were much younger and he and his wife, Dionna, made a conscious effort to prepare them for his time in space. "We decided, as a parental unit, Dionna and I, that we were going to put as much effort into making sure our family was ready as NASA was putting into making sure I was ready to be a crew member," Glover explained. Victor Glover speaking at the Starmus VIII festival in Tenerife, Canary Islands, on Oct. 18, 2026. (Image credit: Daisy Dobrijevic/Future) The family visited NASA's Kennedy Space Center , toured the launch pad and crew quarters and even planned when Glover would call home from the International Space Station . But by the time Artemis II came around, things were different. All four of his daughters were now adults, and preparing them for his journey around the moon meant discussing the mission's risks, including the possibility that he might not return home. Glover recalled his wife telling him something he described as maybe the scariest thing he'd ever heard. "You should have this talk with our daughters." And although he knew she was right, it wasn't an easy conversation to have. "We did, and it did not go well in my opinion," Glover admitted. "Well, it's not about going well. The talk needed to be done, just because it's hard." The following day, Glover sent his daughters and wife a poem, Live Your Life , by Chief Tecumseh. The poem helped Glover express something he had struggled to put into words during their conversation: why he believed the risks of traveling to the moon were worth taking. "It was a very tough conversation, but they understood that I know this is risky. I wasn't just telling them Dad's risking his life. There's a real point to this and there's a reason to take this risk," Glover explained. "This poem helped me to say it in a way that I didn't have words for." After trav

item.title: Gunmen burn seven houses in Plateau community
item.description: …Council chairman condemns attack, promises support for victims By Golok Nanmwa JOS – Gunmen have burnt down seven houses in Bong community, Doemak District of Qua’an-Pan Local Government Area of Plateau State, in a fresh attack that has heightened concerns over insecurity in the state. The attack, which occurred at about 9 p.m. on Sunday, November 15, 2026, reportedly coincided with an assault by suspected terrorists on Zwagal community in Jipal District of neighbouring Mangu Local Government Area, where several people were killed. A community source, Mr Silas Bishop, who confirmed the incident, said the attackers stormed Bong community and set seven houses ablaze. Bishop described the attack as unfortunate and called on security agencies to intensify efforts to track down and arrest those responsible. He also urged the authorities to strengthen surveillance and deploy more security personnel to the community to prevent further attacks. Confirming the incident, the Executive Chairman of Qua’an-Pan Local Government Council, Hon. (Dr.) Christopher Audu Manship, condemned the attack and assured residents that the government would not abandon them. Manship, in a statement signed by his Director of Press and Publicity, Danaan Cletus Sylvanus, on Monday, gave the assurance during an on-the-spot assessment of the destruction in Bong community. He said the government was committed to protecting lives and property across the state. “Government will not abandon the people of Bong community. We will support efforts towards the restoration of the houses destroyed and sustain measures to secure the community against further attacks,” he said. The council chairman also visited Zwagal community in Mangu Local Government Area alongside his Mangu counterpart, Hon. Emmanuel Bala Mwolpun, where he condemned the killing of residents. Describing the attack as barbaric and inhuman, Manship said every human life was precious and that the loss of lives had left lasting pain on the affected families. “The government will intensify efforts to secure lives and property, which remains the primary responsibility of every government,” he said. He urged youths in the affected communities to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious movements to security agencies for necessary action. Manship also said Governor Caleb Mutfwang remained determined to tackle insecurity in Plateau State, adding that the state government was committed to strengthening security measures. He conveyed the governor’s condolences to the bereaved families and residents of Zwagal, while praying for the repose of the souls of those killed. Also speaking, the Mangu Local Government Chairman, Hon. Emmanuel Bala Mwolpun, assured residents that efforts were being made to improve network services in the affected communities to enhance security surveillance and communication. item.title: Atiku mocks presidency over alleged AI-generated rally crowds
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has taken a swipe at President Bola Tinubu over allegations of using artificial intelligence (AI) to create images of campaign crowds, insisting that the massive reception he received in Potiskum, Yobe State, was genuine. Atiku said the reception reflected growing public interest in the African Democratic Congress (ADC)’s Affordable Life campaign, while commending the Yobe State governor for allowing the opposition party to campaign freely in the state. In a statement on Monday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, the former vice president expressed gratitude to residents of Potiskum and Yobe State for the warm reception that greeted his arrival from Azare, Bauchi State. He described the reception as overwhelming, saying the turnout and enthusiasm of residents would remain memorable. “The welcome from the moment we entered Potiskum from Azare was simply breathtaking. The sea of heads, the joyful faces, the chants and the warmth of the people will remain in my heart,” he said. Commending the governor for providing an opportunity for the ADC to engage voters, Atiku said equal access to the electorate was essential to democratic competition. “Democracy is strengthened when every party can meet the people freely and present its message. We appreciate the opportunity to bring our vision to Yobe,” he said. However, taking a swipe at Tinubu, Atiku suggested that the Presidency needed artificial intelligence to create the impression of large campaign crowds, insisting that the supporters who welcomed him in Potiskum were physically present. “The Presidency may need artificial intelligence to conjure a crowd, but in Potiskum the people came out in flesh and blood, unfiltered, unedited and impossible to fabricate. “Our Affordable Life campaign needs no artificial crowd; the people’s presence and their voices speak for themselves,” he said. He further mocked the alleged use of AI-generated images, saying: “The Presidency’s AI must have forgotten that crowds need seats and that people do not fly. Perhaps in Tinubu’s imaginary rally, the supporters were expected to hover through the speech.” On the significance of the “Tinubu Must Go” chants at ADC rallies, Atiku described them as expressions of the people’s desire for change and a reminder of the responsibility that comes with securing their mandate. “The ADC’s Affordable Life campaign is not mere sloganeering. When I hear the crowd chanting ‘Tinubu Must Go’ at our rallies, I take those words personally. “They are a call for change and a reminder of the responsibility that will come with the people’s mandate,” he said. Atiku pledged to prioritise making life affordable for Nigerians if elected president in the January 16, 2027 presidential election. He said his administration would take immediate steps to address the cost-of-living challenges facing Nigerians after Tinubu leaves office on May 29, 2027. “When President Ti

item.title: UEFA backs France’s Diallo to stand against Infantino in FIFA election
item.description: European football’s governing body UEFA has given its “unanimous” backing to French Football Federation chief Philippe Diallo to stand against incumbent Gianni Infantino in March’s FIFA presidential election, it said in a statement Monday. The body said that Diallo had been “invited…to stand as a candidate in the FIFA presidential election in March 2027” and that European national associations had “unanimously pledged their full support”. The deadline for rival candidates to declare themselves is this Wednesday, November 18. UEFA, which boasts 55 member associations, said Diallo “has accepted the invitation to stand” and that his candidature is set to be confirmed at a meeting of the French federation (FFF) on Tuesday. Under its Slovenian president Aleksander Ceferin, UEFA has led the opposition to Infantino since his announcement in late July of a project to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors. Infantino quickly abandoned the proposal in the face of widespread uproar, but UEFA has since gone to a court in Florida in an attempt to gather evidence for a potential complaint of “criminal mismanagement” against the FIFA president in Switzerland. UEFA had been struggling to find a credible candidate to stand against Infantino in the election, which will take place at the FIFA Congress on March 18 next year in the Moroccan capital, Rabat. – Wenger not in running – Arsene Wenger, the French former Arsenal manager and FIFA’s current chief of global football development, had been seen as a potential candidate that could get Europe’s backing. One source within football governance said that Wenger had been UEFA’s “Plan A” and that Diallo had never been seen as a solution before it became clear the ex-Arsenal boss would not be a candidate. CONCACAF chief Victor Montagliani had previously been mooted as a candidate, but the Canadian later announced his desire to stand for a new term as the head of his confederation, which covers North and Central America and the Caribbean. The Asian Football Confederation, which consists of 47 member associations, announced last month that it was backing Infantino for re-election. Diallo said in September that the FFF was withdrawing its backing for Infantino in the election, following similar announcements from other European associations. “We believe that the trust placed in the FIFA president has been betrayed, and that the way in which the governance of world football is envisaged no longer reflects us,” he said at the time. Diallo, the 63-year-old son of a Senegalese boxing champion, has been president of the FFF since January 2023. He was initially appointed to the post on an interim basis when previous chief Noel Le Graet was forced to stand down following a series of controversies. Diallo, from Saint-Nazaire on France’s Atlantic coast, was then elected to the role by a large majority in June of that year, before being re-elected in December 2024 for a new four-year term. item.title: Police arrest 8 over APC, NDC clash in Kano
item.description: The Kano State Police Command has arrested eight suspects following a clash between supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the New Democratic Congress (NDC) in Bichi Local Government Area of the state. The command’s spokesman, CSP Abdullahi Kiyawa, disclosed this in a statement on Monday in Kano, saying the incident occurred at about 4:45 p.m. on Sunday. He said the clash resulted in the destruction of campaign banners, billboards and vehicles, while some persons sustained injuries. According to him, police operatives were immediately deployed to the area after receiving reports of the incident and successfully restored normalcy. Kiyawa disclosed that 13 vehicles were vandalised during the clash, while five injured persons were taken to hospital for treatment. Items recovered by the police included one Gariyo, two cutlasses, two hard sticks, a bottle of solution and a substance locally known as “Suck and Die”. He quoted the Commissioner of Police, Ibrahim Bakori, as condemning the violence and destruction of campaign materials by political supporters. Bakori warned that the command would not tolerate any act capable of disrupting public peace before, during or after the political season. He urged political leaders and their supporters to conduct their activities peacefully and in accordance with the law. The police spokesman said the eight suspects had been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID) for discreet investigation. He added that the suspects would be charged to court upon completion of the investigation. Kiyawa urged political leaders, party supporters and members of the public to shun violence and report suspicious activities to the nearest police station. He said the area remained relatively calm, while police monitoring continued. NAN The post Police arrest 8 over APC, NDC clash in Kano appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Microsoft fixes Windows activation as admins pick through Exchange outage wreckage
item.description: Microsoft has released an out-of-band update to fix licensing and activation errors introduced by November's Windows security update. The fix is available from the Microsoft Update Catalog for Windows Server 2025, 2022, and 2019, Windows 10 22H2 ESU, and Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2021 and 2019. Windows 11 23H2 users can obtain it from the Catalog or through Windows Update's Optional updates menu. The "non-security OOB update" targets affected enterprise devices. Microsoft stated: "Certain Windows licensing and activation operations using the Software Licensing Management Tool (SLMGR) might fail with error 0x80041008 (Invalid parameter). "This primarily affects organizations using slmgr.vbs commands or automated processes to configure Key Management Service (KMS) activation, install product keys, or manage Windows licensing." Devices that are already activated will remain activated, Microsoft said. Breaking the machinery customers use to activate paid-for software is a bad look for a Patch Tuesday release . Administrators may wonder how Microsoft's updates are tested when installing one means waiting for another to repair the damage. Those same administrators may also have been fielding calls about last week's widespread Exchange Online outage, which Microsoft has partly attributed to a defect it introduced in July . On top of that, Microsoft told administrators just days ago to consider unsupported Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 " permanently vulnerable ." Exchange Online avoids that particular support deadline, but the recent outage was a reminder that handing over the servers doesn't make software defects disappear. Forget "security by obscurity." Last week's approach was more like "security by unavailability." Between getting Windows activated and keeping Exchange Online online, Microsoft gave administrators plenty to do. None of it was likely to feature in their original plans for the week. Not all the glitches introduced by November's Patch Tuesday have yet been resolved, as some customers using a Windows device to print will be aware. ®

item.title: KASU unions suspend strike, insist on welfare demands
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo The Joint Action Committee (JAC) of Kaduna State University (KASU) has suspended its one-week warning strike following discussions with key stakeholders in the Kaduna State Government and the university management. The unions, however, said the suspension did not amount to abandoning their demands, insisting that outstanding welfare issues and agreements with the government must be fully addressed. JAC Chairperson, Sa’adiyya Mustapha, announced the suspension on Monday, explaining that the decision was taken to allow ongoing negotiations to continue and pave the way for an amicable resolution of the dispute. The committee comprises the Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities (SSANU), the Non-Academic Staff Union of Educational and Associated Institutions (NASU) and the National Association of Academic Technologists (NAAT). Mustapha said the unions suspended the strike in the interest of the university after key stakeholders in the state government intervened and initiated discussions with them. “We have gone on a one-week strike and have now decided to suspend it, not because we are surrendering, but for the good of this university. “Several key stakeholders in this administration have made efforts to dialogue with us, and we have seen reason in those discussions. We have therefore decided to suspend the strike to show that we are willing to support the government and give dialogue a chance,” she said. She commended union members for their support and resilience during the industrial action, noting that the strike was intended to draw attention to their unresolved grievances. The JAC chairperson also reaffirmed the unions’ support for Governor Uba Sani, recalling previous salary-related challenges faced by university workers and the governor’s intervention in clearing outstanding payments. According to her, workers received half salaries in 2017, while their May 2023 salaries remained unpaid until the outstanding payments were presented to the governor and subsequently cleared after he assumed office. “Because of what he has done for us, we cannot say we are not in support of him. We support the governor and are solidly behind him. “However, what happened to JAC was what we were unhappy with, and that was why we decided to embark on the strike,” she said. Mustapha expressed optimism that the ongoing negotiations would produce positive results, urging the university management, governing council and state government to ensure fairness and equity in their dealings with staff. The industrial action followed a seven-day ultimatum issued by the three unions on November 2, 2026, to the Kaduna State Government and the university management over outstanding welfare demands and alleged failure to implement agreements reached with non-teaching staff unions. item.title: Beyoncé Becomes First Artiste To Reach 100 Grammy Nominations
item.description: American singer Beyoncé has become the first artiste in Grammy Awards history to receive 100 career nominations, extending her record as the most-nominated artiste in the award’s history. The milestone came with the announcement of the nominees for the 69th Annual Grammy Awards on Monday, November 16, 2026, following her nomination in the Best R&B Solo Performance category for her song ‘Morning Dew (Donk)’. The latest recognition takes Beyoncé’s nomination tally to 100, further widening her lead over other artistes, including her husband, rapper Jay-Z, who previously held the record alongside her. Beyoncé entered the Grammy nominations list in 2000 as a member of Destiny’s Child, earning nominations for ‘Bills, Bills, Bills’ in the Best R&B Song and Best R&B Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals categories. She subsequently built a record-breaking career across several genres, including R&B, pop, dance and electronic music, and country. This cover image released by Parkwood/Columbia/Sony shows “Cowboy Carter” by Beyoncé. Her latest nomination is for ‘Morning Dew (Donk)’, a previously unreleased recording from the sessions for her second studio album, ‘B’Day,’ released in 2006. The song was released on July 4, 2026, ahead of the album’s 20th anniversary, and later featured on its deluxe anniversary edition. Beyoncé and Pharrell Williams produced the track, which was written by the singer alongside Williams, The-Dream and Darius Dixon. Other nominees in the Best R&B Solo Performance category are Kehlani for ‘Out the Window’, Victoria Monét for ‘Let Me’, Jill Scott for ‘Pressha’ and Tems for ‘What You Need’. Beyond her nomination record, Beyoncé remains the most-awarded artiste in Grammy history, with 35 wins. A large Grammy award is seen outside the press room during the 62nd Annual Grammy Awards on January 26, 2020, in Los Angeles. (Photo by Frederic J. BROWN / AFP) She broke the record in 2023 after winning four awards at the 65th Grammy Awards, taking her total to 32 and surpassing the previous record of 31 held by classical conductor Georg Solti. She added three more awards in 2025. At the 67th Grammy Awards in 2025, Beyoncé also won Album of the Year and Best Country Album for ‘Cowboy Carter,’becoming the first Black woman to win the latter category. The 69th Grammy Awards ceremony is scheduled to hold on February 7, 2027, at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, California. The post Beyoncé Becomes First Artiste To Reach 100 Grammy Nominations appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Budget 2027: FG moves to cut overhead, orders MDAs to share facilities
item.description: …Targets spending on hotels, private venues for official meetings By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Federal Government has directed Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) to maximise the use of existing government-owned facilities instead of spending public funds on hotels and other privately owned venues for official meetings, as part of efforts to reduce overhead expenditure in the 2027 Budget. The move is part of a broader cost-saving initiative by the Federal Ministry of Finance, through its Efficiency Office (E-Office), to eliminate avoidable expenditure, improve the utilisation of public assets and ensure value for money in government operations. The Head of the Ministry’s Information and Public Relations Unit, Efe Ovuakporie, disclosed this in a statement issued in Abuja on Monday. She said the Efficiency Office was working towards establishing a coordinated system that would enable MDAs to identify and access available meeting and conference facilities across government institutions, thereby reducing the need to hire commercial venues for official engagements. According to her, a major component of the initiative is the compilation of a comprehensive directory of meeting facilities owned by MDAs nationwide. The directory, which will be published on the Federal Ministry of Finance’s website upon completion, is expected to provide government institutions with information on available facilities and make it easier for them to locate suitable venues. Ovuakporie explained that the arrangement would also enable MDAs with underutilised conference facilities to generate revenue by making them available to other government institutions, while reducing pressure on government overhead budgets. She said the initiative aligned with the Efficiency Office’s mandate to promote value for money, reduce overhead expenditure, monitor the utilisation of public assets and identify areas of waste across government institutions. In a related development, the Efficiency Office recently inspected shared government facilities across the five South-East states of Abia, Anambra, Ebonyi, Enugu and Imo to identify underutilised public infrastructure and opportunities for cost savings. The inspection covered selected Federal Secretariats, Federal Polytechnics, Federal Medical Centres and Federal Universities. According to the statement, the exercise assessed the condition, availability, utilisation and maintenance of the facilities, with particular attention to areas where improved management could enhance productivity and reduce unnecessary government spending. The inspection teams identified underutilised office spaces and facilities, deteriorating furniture, fittings and equipment, as well as inadequate maintenance of some offices and common areas. They also identified opportunities to improve the use of conference facilities and strengthen the organisation, storage and preservation of official records. item.title: Crook turns free trials into phishing factory, as LearnWorlds sends 13,000 fake YouTube copyright notices
item.description: LearnWorlds, a software and learning course platform, says an attacker sent 13,000 phishing emails to customers over seven days by using automated tools to open free trial accounts. The company insists its systems were not breached. Panos Siozos, Co-founder and CEO at LearnWorlds, said the miscreant created around 570 free trial accounts on the platform between November 7-14, which they used to issue fake copyright infringement notices to customers. "We have found no evidence of unauthorized access to existing customer schools or personal data held for our customers and their end users," he told The Register . According to Siozos, the attacker bypassed the platform's per-customer limit on trial subscriptions and exploited its welcome email feature to send the phishing emails. "In each trial they added their own list of target addresses and rewrote the standard welcome email as a fake copyright notice," he said. "Adding those users triggered the welcome email from our sending address." The first email was sent on November 7, after which the company detected the suspicious signups and blocked the first sender on November 9, although the attacker returned to send a second wave of emails within 40 minutes. LearnWorlds removed all the trial accounts by November 10 and one paid account, which was used to launch more emails, on November 14. "In total, around 13,000 emails were sent to addresses on external recipient lists supplied by the sender," said Siozos. "The trial accounts sent 9,853 between November 7-9, and the paid account sent 3,723 on November 14. "We can’t tell how many people clicked, because the link was disguised to hide clicks. The recipient addresses were the sender’s own list." The CEO confirmed that LearnWorlds has since enhanced its bot checks and is placing holds on new accounts if their emails trigger fraud flags. "We have also examined the novel patterns the attackers used to create more advanced scoring mechanisms. We have reported the phishing website so it can be taken down. Further measures are currently being examined. "Anyone who signed in on the fake page should change their Google password and review their account’s recent security activity." The company's confirmation follows suspicions of foul play aired by users on social media. User reports included copies of the emails they received, which demanded urgent responses to fake copyright infringement claims related to YouTube content. Among the more prominent recipients of the copyright infringement email notices was Marcus Hutchins, of WannaCry fame , who claimed he received an email from the company’s official mail server. The email, a copy of which Hutchins posted to X , referenced general intellectual property and copyright infringements but failed to specify any specific issues. item.title: How I used evidence and imagination to write an account of the world in 2096
item.description: Fatih Aktas/Anadolu Agency via Getty Images How do you invent the future? This isn’t a question that I had ever had to consider until I set out to imagine what the world would be like in 70 years’ time for New Scientist ’s 70th anniversary. As a lifelong sci-fi nerd, I have read and watched loads of material that could have served as inspiration. But this being New Scientist , I wanted to make sure that I was as grounded in real science and technology as possible – while acknowledging that no prediction of the future is ever correct. I began by asking my colleagues on the magazine for their ideas about the future and then attempted to corral this sci-fi smorgasbord into something resembling an outline of a self-consistent narrative. Part of the problem in imagining many different futures is that they contradict themselves – you can’t have the war-torn AI dystopia of Terminator alongside the utopia of Star Trek . I wanted both hope and realism in my future, so I decided to look at how the scientific literature handles the end of the century. One of the most obvious forecasts is for climate change, where we have a pretty good idea about what might happen in 2096, under a range of scenarios, because it all boils down to atmospheric physics that we can model. Of course, which of these scenarios we end up with is all too dependent on human politics, so the science alone couldn’t guide me. I also turned to population projections , which, for the most part, are locked in based on current population trends. The idea that the end of the century will be the first time we are living in a world of falling populations became a fascinating strand in the final piece. Advertisement The biggest problem I faced was how to deal with AI. I am not confident making predictions on this topic even just a few years in advance – as I’ve written previously, my views on AI have evolved between the release of ChatGPT in 2022 and now , so how could I possibly predict what would happen by the time we got to 2096? Furthermore, there was a risk that AI could come to dominate the piece, crowding out everything else. There is a graph I often think about, published by the Financial Times under the headline “AI could end scarcity, end humanity – or boost [GDP] growth by 0.2 percentage points”. I knew that, to preserve any meaningful narrative, I had to restrict AI to this boring middle option, so I invented an AI-fuelled financial crisis that would see us place limits on the technology. I have no idea if such an event is likely to happen, but it seems to me to be the only way to preserve a future that remains comprehensible to us today. I spoke to dozens of experts to help inform this piece, expecting them to contradict each other in ways that were both helpful and confounding, and they did. But what I found most interesting is how little interdisciplinary forecasting there is across science. For example, attempts to predict future public health trends are only just starting to cons

item.title: The Leonid meteor shower peaks Nov. 17-18! Here's what you need to know
item.description: null The Leonid meteor shower peaks Nov. 17-18 sending shooting stars and fireballs across the autumn sky as Earth passes through a stream of debris left by Comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle. Up to 15 meteors could be spotted per hour under perfect dark sky conditions on the night of Nov. 17-18, according to the International Meteor Organisation . NASA, meanwhile, has given a more conservative rate of less than three meteors per hour — time will tell. Leonid meteors appear to race away from a point of origin, or radiant, in the constellation Leo, which glistens high above the southeastern horizon in the hours before dawn in mid-November. Both Jupiter and Mars will be separated by just a few degrees in the constellation Leo on the night of the peak, making it particularly easy to find in 2026! When is the best time to look for Leonid meteors? The best time to spot Leonids is in the hours before dawn on Nov. 18, when the radiant will reach its highest point in the southeastern sky, maximizing the amount of meteors that may be seen skimming through Earth's atmosphere . By then, the waxing moon will have set, leaving darker skies and a better chance of spotting fainter meteors. Shooting stars that appear close to the radiant will strike Earth almost head-on, leaving the shortest trails. Instead, find a patch of sky a short distance away from the constellation Leo, where the meteors will be at their most impressive, and give your eyes 20-30 minutes to fully adapt to the dark. Why are the Leonids special? As if shooting stars weren't enough, the Leonid shower is also known for spawning dazzling fireballs and long-lasting Earth-grazing meteors , which strike our atmosphere at an oblique angle, leaving long trains as they skim through before passing back out into space. The shower is also capable of producing magnificent meteor storms when Earth passes through particularly dense trails of debris left behind by Comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, which orbits the sun approximately every 33 years. Sadly, we'll have to wait a bit for the next big show. According to the Planetary Society , another Leonid meteor storm could occur as early as 2031, while a study released in August 2026 predicts potentially spectacular displays in 2033 and 2034. Want to photograph a shooting star? Then be sure to read our guide to imaging shooting stars , along with our selections of the best lenses and cameras for astrophotography on the market in 2026. Editor's Note: If you would like to share your Leonid photos with Space.com's readers, then please send your photo(s), comments, and your name and location to spacephotos@space.com.

To be clear, nothing has been confirmed about the status of a third The Batman movie, but the latest news combined with the extreme delays facing The Batman Part II feel like a pretty clear indication that the Batmobile has hit a dead end and will need yet another reboot.

item.title: Lagos PDP candidate promises tax exemption for teachers, doctors
item.description: By Cynthia Alo & Kafayat Kokumo The Lagos State governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Adedeji Doherty, has promised to exempt teachers and doctors from paying taxes if elected governor, saying his administration would deploy increased federal allocations to improve healthcare, education and residents’ welfare. Doherty made the pledge during an interview on Channels Television on Monday, where he also proposed a special tax card that would allow residents unable to afford the existing tax burden to pay N10,000 annually and enjoy subsidies on drugs and transportation. He said his proposed policy would ensure that increased revenue accruing to the state translated into direct benefits for residents. “When I am governor, I will definitely transfer these palliatives, these subsidies to my people. For instance, the doctors will not pay tax. For instance, the teachers will not pay tax. Those two people will not pay tax,” he said. Explaining the proposed tax card, Doherty said residents who could not afford to pay N50,000 annually would be allowed to pay N10,000 and benefit from subsidised medication and transportation. “Out of this N250 billion plus, I will transfer it into cards, whereby for those that cannot pay N50,000 per year in tax, I will create a card that you can pay N10,000 per year in tax, but you will get a subsidy in your drugs and you will get a subsidy in your transportation. “This is giving money back to the people of Lagos State because I have it. Mr President has given it to me and I am giving it to you,” he said. The PDP candidate also promised to introduce free education, arguing that the resources available to Lagos State would enable his administration to implement the policy. He justified his proposed tax exemption for doctors by citing an alleged shortage of medical personnel in the state, claiming that Lagos had about 3,000 doctors against an estimated requirement of 15,000. “We need close to about 15,000 doctors in Lagos State as we speak, but right now we have only about 3,000. So, if 3,000 doctors are not paying tax, please give me a break,” he said. Doherty also promised improved welfare packages, including comfortable accommodation, discounted food and car loans, to encourage medical professionals practising abroad to return to Lagos. “I want those experts in London, in America, in Germany, in Hungary. I want them to come back to Lagos and feel like they are even special. I will make them special, just like the teachers,” he said. He described teachers as critical to the future of the state, stressing the need to provide them with adequate training and support to prepare children for leadership and professional responsibilities. On his campaign activities, the governorship candidate condemned attacks on political materials, alleging that some individuals he described as area boys had pulled down his campaign posters around Oregun and the Third Mainland Bridge. The big sale also extends to headsets , console covers , and even Sony’s 27-inch monitor that has a hook to charge your controller. item.title: 2027: I want to deliver Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda in Lagos, says PDP’s Doherty
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Lagos State, Adedeji Doherty, has described President Bola Ahmed Tinubu as his National Leader, saying he is contesting against the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, to ensure that the President’s Renewed Hope agenda is properly implemented in the state. Doherty stated this on Monday during an interview on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily, where he explained why he was seeking to become Lagos governor despite his support for Tinubu and his administration’s national agenda. He said he supported Tinubu’s Renewed Hope agenda but disagreed with the way the APC-led government in Lagos State was implementing it. According to him, the failure to translate the President’s vision into reality in Lagos had contributed to political tensions, including alleged thuggery and the destruction of campaign materials. He said, “I am going against the APC governorship candidate in Lagos because they are not doing what they are supposed to do concerning the APC/Mr President’s agenda for the country. “When you do not crystallise the dream that is being made by your boss, then definitely all these fallouts of thuggery, removing of banners, tearing of posters and things like that, definitely is what is going to happen because you are trying to cover up your inadequacies in government.” The PDP candidate further described Tinubu as his National Leader, stressing that his support for the President and the Renewed Hope agenda did not extend to the way the agenda was being implemented in Lagos. He said, “Basically, you know? I’m going to support what I support fully, what my National Leader is doing. I support fully the Renewed Hope agenda, which is the agenda for the entire country, but I do not support the agenda as it is being materialised and crystallised in Lagos State.” The post 2027: I want to deliver Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda in Lagos, says PDP’s Doherty appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: UK actor Robert Pattinson to be new James Bond
item.description: British actor Robert Pattinson was Monday named as the new James Bond, stepping into the coveted role of the world’s most famous fictional spy. “Amazon MGM Studios have announced that Robert Pattinson will take on the iconic role of James Bond,” the studio said on the official 007.com website. Pattinson would succeed Daniel Craig as the super-suave MI6 agent, “ushering in a new era for one of cinema’s most celebrated characters”, the studios added. It will be the first Bond film since long-term Bond producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael Wilson stepped back and Amazon took creative control of the franchise, after acquiring the series’ parent company MGM. “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime,” Pattinson said. “To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement,” he added in a statement. Amazon MGM also announced that Oscar-nominated Canadian director Denis Villeneuve, behind such box-office hits as the “Dune” films, would be directing the next Bond movie from a script by “Peaky Blinders” creator Steven Knight. Knight said in May that Amazon has given him a licence to play with the legendary secret agent created by author Ian Fleming. “Bond has been bulletproof. People have been able to make mistakes and variations, and the character has survived,” Knight told Screen magazine at the Cannes Film Festival. “Because the core of it is like a diamond. You can’t touch it,” he added. Knight also told reporters that he has done research with “the SAS and even more secret outfits” for his reinvention of the next 007 movie. Pattinson, 40, started out in amateur dramatics before getting his break in “Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire” (2005) as Cedric Diggory, a champion for Hogwarts. But he rocketed to global fame for his part as brooding teen heartthrob in the romantic vampire saga “Twilight”. – ‘Extremely inventive’ – He was paid a reported $2 million for his lead in “Twilight” (2008), but by the time the saga wrapped up with the two parts of “Breaking Dawn” in 2011 and 2012, he was reportedly on $12.5 million plus 7.5 percent of the box office take. One of his first forays into edgier cinema came with 2012 drama “Cosmopolis”, in which he portrayed a self-destructive currency speculator as his life falls apart. The film was directed by legendary US auteur David Cronenberg, who described the actor as “extremely inventive”. He received critical acclaim after later switching to more independent films and was nominated for best actor at the Cannes festival in 2017 for neo-grindhouse crime caper “Good Time” by New York-based brothers Josh and Ben Safdie. In 2022, Amazon bought storied Hollywood studio MGM, which held distribution rights to Bond’s extensive back catalogue. But it was not until early 2025 that the company struck a deal with longtime Bond producers Wilson and Broccoli to obtain full creative control. The franchise had been closely guarded by the Broccoli f

item.title: US now "comfortable" with children dying of measles as death toll hits 10
item.description: Health officials in Pennsylvania and Wisconsin announced two more measles deaths late last week, bringing the national tally of confirmed measles deaths this year to 10. The total includes the deaths of at least four infants: two in Pennsylvania , one in New York , and one in Wisconsin . Wisconsin health officials said the latest measles death—the second for the state—was in a child. Pennsylvania's health department did not reveal the age or other details of the latest death—the state's seventh—besides revealing it was of an unvaccinated resident in Montour County. Overall, the seven deaths in Pennsylvania include two in Jefferson County, three in Lancaster County, and one in Mifflin, in addition to the new death in Montour. An eighth death was reported in Franklin County , but state health officials have not confirmed it. For all the states with deaths so far, health officials have noted that they're the first deaths in decades. Multiple outbreaks are underway across the country, pushing the national tally of cases to nearly 5,500 across 47 states and jurisdictions, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Pennsylvania's case count alone is over 1,500, and Wisconsin is reporting nearly 650. Read full article Comments

item.title: INEC debunks claim of remote BVAS log-out before voting ends
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has dismissed as false and misleading a viral social media video alleging that the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) would be remotely logged out before the end of voting. The commission clarified that only the poll official operating the device has the authority to log in or log out of the BVAS during voter accreditation and the subsequent result upload process. INEC disclosed this in a statement posted on its official X platform on Monday, following the circulation of a video on Instagram alleging that voters would be logged out of the system before the conclusion of voting. Describing the claim as fabricated, the commission said each polling unit was assigned unique login credentials, which were issued to the Presiding Officer on the eve of an election. According to INEC, the credentials enable the poll official to log into the BVAS for voter accreditation on election day and subsequently upload the polling unit result sheet at the close of polls. “The claim that the BVAS can be remotely logged out before the conclusion of accreditation and voting is false,” the commission stated. It stressed that there was no provision for any external individual or authority to remotely log out the device. The commission also dismissed claims that election results uploaded offline could be lost, explaining that the IReV application had been upgraded to accommodate offline uploads. INEC said the enhancement followed experiences during the 2023 general election, when some poll officials were held hostage at their polling units because they could not upload results due to poor or non-existent network connectivity. It explained that the offline upload feature allows poll officials in areas with poor or no network coverage to upload polling unit result sheets in the presence of stakeholders at the polling unit. According to the commission, such results remain securely stored on the BVAS pending successful transmission to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV). ” As Poll Officials proceed from the polling unit to the Ward Collation Centre and the device reconnects to the internet, the result sheet is automatically transmitted to the IReV portal without requiring any further manual intervention,” it said. INEC assured Nigerians that the BVAS and IReV systems operate in accordance with established procedures designed to protect the integrity, transparency and credibility of the electoral process. The commission urged members of the public to disregard the video, refrain from creating or sharing unverified information and rely on its official communication channels for accurate information. It reaffirmed its commitment to transparency, accountability and the conduct of free, fair and credible elections. The post INEC debunks claim of remote BVAS log-out before voting ends appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Russia's war on Ukraine: 'Americans want to have a deal whatever the cost for both Ukraine & Europe'

As European countries prepare to take part in the next round of Ukraine peace talks, Roos questions whether having five European representatives could weaken their negotiating position. "The other option is to realize that it dilutes the negotiating power of Europe. And I would lean towards that," he says, proposing Finnish President Alexander Stubb as a possible representative. Roos also points to differences between Washington and European governments over negotiations with Russia. While "the Americans do absolutely want to have a deal whatever the cost for both Ukraine and Europe," he argues that European governments have little choice but to maintain pressure on Moscow, which has yet to abandon its "maximalist demands."

item.title: Plateau records 5,457 suspected diabetes cases in nine months
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS — The Plateau State Government has raised concerns over the growing burden of diabetes in the state, following the record of 5,457 suspected new cases between January and September 2026. The Commissioner for Health, Dr Nicholas Ba’amlong, disclosed this on Monday during a press briefing in Jos to commemorate the 2026 World Diabetes Day. Ba’amlong said the figure followed 5,546 suspected cases recorded in 2025, but clarified that the numbers represented suspected cases and not confirmed diagnoses. He said diabetes remained a major public health concern because many people were living with the condition without knowing their status. The commissioner also disclosed that findings from the 2024 nationwide Know Your Number, Control Your Number screening campaign showed that 14,359 people were screened in Plateau State, with 2,610, representing approximately 18 per cent, recording elevated blood glucose levels. He, however, cautioned that the findings did not represent the prevalence of diabetes in the state. According to him, the figures underscore the need to expand access to screening, diagnosis and treatment services. As part of activities marking this year’s World Diabetes Day, the Ministry of Health, in collaboration with the Plateau State chapters of the Diabetes Association of Nigeria and the Endocrine and Metabolic Society of Nigeria, conducted a free workplace screening exercise at the Joseph Gomwalk Secretariat Complex, Jos. Ba’amlong said the exercise targeted 1,000 civil servants and provided blood glucose and blood pressure checks, weight and body mass index assessments, health education, counselling and referrals for further medical attention where necessary. Speaking on government interventions, the commissioner said the administration of Governor Caleb Mutfwang was working towards extending diabetes education and screening services to underserved communities across the state’s 17 local government areas through existing primary healthcare facilities and community outreach programmes. He added that the government was exploring partnerships and appropriate medical technologies to improve access to diagnostic services, particularly at the primary healthcare level, while strengthening follow-up and referral systems for people with elevated blood glucose levels. “Screening is only the beginning. Early detection must lead to appropriate diagnosis and treatment,” he said. The commissioner urged residents, particularly those with a family history of diabetes, excess weight or high blood pressure, to check their blood glucose levels regularly and seek medical attention when necessary. He also advised residents to adopt healthy lifestyles through balanced diets, regular physical activity and weight management, while avoiding tobacco and limiting alcohol consumption. Ba’amlong identified excessive thirst, frequent urination, unexplained weight loss and persistent fatigue as some of the symptoms that could indicate diabetes. He f

item.title: Ejiofor hails DSS DG over evacuation of Igbo youths from Wawa facility
item.description: By Nwabueze Okonkwo ONITSHA — Human rights lawyer, Sir Ifeanyi Ejiofor, has commended the Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS), Oluwatosin Adeola Ajayi, for reforms at the Wawa detention facility and the evacuation of a significant number of Igbo youths from the facility. Ejiofor also praised Ajayi for what he described as an end to the alleged arbitrary arrest and abduction of Igbo youths, which he claimed had become frequent under the previous leadership of the Service. The lawyer made the commendation in a statement on Monday titled, “Wawa Barracks: The horrifying testimonies of survivors of enforced disappearances under the Buhari regime — a time for Igbos to introspect”. He expressed concern over alleged abuses at the detention facility, including arbitrary arrests, torture, deprivation of medical attention and deaths, based on accounts he attributed to former detainees. According to him, the situation had at some point deteriorated to the extent that some individuals of Igbo extraction allegedly exploited security agencies to settle personal scores. He said the reported reforms under Ajayi had helped restore confidence and a measure of security in the South-East. “Happily, that dark chapter has been brought to an end, restoring confidence, peace and a measure of security in the South-East geopolitical zone,” he said. Ejiofor described the alleged experiences of detainees as disturbing, claiming that many Igbo youths had suffered under the previous DSS leadership. He, however, stressed that his criticism of alleged security abuses should not be interpreted as support for criminal activities by non-state actors operating in the region. ” No grievance, however genuine, confers a licence for criminality; equally, no allegation of criminality confers a licence for lawlessness by the State,” he said. The lawyer appealed to the DSS Director-General to facilitate the release of more detainees who, according to him, had no involvement in criminal activities and against whom there was no credible evidence of wrongdoing. He also urged the Service to withdraw charges allegedly founded on ethnic profiling, arguing that addressing the underlying causes of agitation was more important than sustaining what he described as prejudicial ethnic categorisation. Ejiofor further commended Ajayi for what he called commendable reforms within the Service, saying the intervention demonstrated the importance of professionalism and institutional changes in rebuilding public confidence. He called for an end to the use of propaganda as a security strategy, arguing that public trust could only be restored through justice, accountability and respect for citizens’ rights. The lawyer also urged the Igbo people to reflect on the crisis, warning against internal divisions and the exploitation of collective grievances by individuals seeking personal benefits. item.title: US allies deepen deal to guard AI supply chains against 'hostile actors' (cough, China, cough)
item.description: Nine countries including the UK have signed a US declaration pledging to secure supply chains for AI tech, as pressure grows for tighter export controls following the high-profile resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang . The US is firming up its Pax Silica initiative on AI and supply chain security. Under the San Francisco declaration , signed on November 15, the coalition says it is entering a new phase that turns shared principles into a working partnership with shared responsibilities. Pax Silica was announced in December last year, ostensibly for the participants to work together on vital parts of the global technology supply chain, including frontier foundation models, compute and semiconductors, advanced manufacturing, minerals refining and processing, and energy. But the list of participants was notable for not including one country – China – leading many to suspect that Pax Silica is yet another effort by Washington to squeeze out its main rival in the global technology and economic stakes. Hong-Kong based South China Morning Post refers to it as Trump's "campaign to China-proof AI and chip supply chains." The latest declaration states that "the security of our peoples cannot be separated from the security of our economies and those of our closest partners," and sets out what must be protected, as well as committing to "protect it together." It asserts that protection should cover key foundational technologies essential to economic security, listing "software, materials, knowledge, components and inputs…essential to AI supply chains." This includes anything that "theft, illicit transfer, or acquisition by hostile actors would confer a meaningful military or intelligence advantage, or undue economic leverage over the participants, or whose unauthorized transfer or misuse could pose significant risks to the economic and national security of the participants." Also listed is the protection of critical infrastructure such as ports, terminals, transport, communications, and logistics networks, and the ICT and energy infrastructure these depend upon. The declaration was jointly released by the US administration, and the governments of Australia, India, Israel, Japan, South Korea, Qatar, Singapore, United Arab Emirates, and the United Kingdom. "The know-how to design a chip, the machine that makes it, and the port that ships it can all be in different countries," the US under-secretary of state for economic affairs Jacob Helberg told the Financial Times . "What makes the San Francisco Declaration historic is that Pax Silica partners have agreed to treat the security of those technologies and the infrastructure behind them as a shared responsibility." This move comes amid reports that both Republican and Democrat lawmakers want to push through further measures to prevent China from accessing advanced chips for AI processing. item.title: 2027: Shehu Buba inaugurates 1,000-member campaign council
item.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The governorship candidate of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) in Bauchi State, Senator Shehu Buba Umar, has inaugurated a 1,000-member campaign council ahead of the 2027 general elections, urging members to embrace unity, peaceful political engagement and issue-based campaigns. Buba, who represents Bauchi South Senatorial District in the National Assembly, inaugurated the council on Sunday, with members drawn from the 20 local government areas of the state. He described the inauguration as a major step towards strengthening the party’s grassroots mobilisation, coordinating its political activities and improving its chances in the 2027 governorship election. The senator said the council comprised experienced party stakeholders and directors representing the various senatorial districts and local government areas, with the responsibility of developing strategies and coordinating campaign activities. He urged members to set aside personal differences and work collectively towards the party’s victory, stressing that political disagreements should be resolved through dialogue, persuasion and mutual understanding. Buba warned against violence, slander and character assassination, insisting that electoral victory could only be achieved through constructive engagement with voters and the presentation of credible alternatives. He said his ambition to govern Bauchi State was driven by the desire to address what he described as challenges of misgovernance and redirect the state towards sustainable development and prosperity. According to him, his development agenda will focus on economic stability and growth, improved security, urban and rural infrastructure, people-oriented reforms and the general welfare of residents. The PRP candidate also emphasised the importance of grassroots mobilisation, adequate electoral preparation and voter education, particularly on the need for voters to protect their votes after casting their ballots. He noted that effective governance would require cooperation between the executive and legislative arms of government, expressing the need for the PRP to secure representation in the State House of Assembly and National Assembly to facilitate the implementation of its manifesto. Describing the 2027 contest as challenging, Buba charged members of the campaign council to develop a workable programme and adopt strategies capable of securing victory for the party. He urged them to take the campaign to communities, wards and polling units, listen to residents’ concerns and communicate the party’s programmes and policies to the electorate. He further insisted that the PRP’s campaign should be guided by respect for voters and issue-based engagement rather than unnecessary attacks on political opponents. Expressing confidence in the party’s chances, Buba identified unity, commitment, hard work and popular support as critical factors for victory. item.title: 2027: Tinubu, Oborevwori assured of victory in Delta — Olejeme
item.description: By Precious Enaike The Zonal Director, South-South Election Planning, Coordination, Monitoring and Mobilisation of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Dr. Ngozi Olejeme, has expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu, Delta State Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and other APC candidates will win the 2027 general elections. Olejeme attributed her optimism to what she described as the growing strength of grassroots mobilisation within the party’s campaign structure, particularly in Oshimili South Local Government Area of Delta State. She spoke at the Oshimili South Arcade, Asaba, where she joined other party leaders in welcoming Oborevwori, his deputy, Sir Monday Onyeme, former Governor Ifeanyi Okowa and other members of the State Campaign Council to the local government. The former boss of the Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF) assured the governor that her council was prepared to mobilise support for all APC candidates in the area. Addressing party supporters, traders, youths and other residents at the rally, Olejeme expressed confidence that sustained grassroots engagement would translate into overwhelming electoral support for the APC. She said, “My Governor, we are here to tell you that Tinubu has already won. All APC candidates have already won. Mr. Governor, Oshimili South is the capital of government, and we trust and believe in you. “Based on the work we have done so far at the grassroots, I can assure you that we have already delivered President Tinubu and you, our confirmed Governor.” Olejeme, however, urged residents and party supporters to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), stressing that grassroots mobilisation must be backed by active participation in the electoral process. “I have only one request to make: Go and make sure you collect your PVC. Your PVC is what will give us this victory. Collect your PVC; it is very important because we are already set for victory. We have reached our promised land, and your PVC is of immense importance at this point,” she said. She described Oborevwori as a performing governor who had exceeded expectations, while applauding Tinubu for what she called his achievements in office. Olejeme urged Nigerians to give the President another mandate in 2027, arguing that his performance deserved a second term. “Our Governor has performed very well. Governor Oborevwori is the best in Africa. President Tinubu has done so much that the people are not talking about. For the good work he has done, we have to give him more work to do by re-electing him in the 2027 general election,” she said. She expressed confidence that Tinubu, Oborevwori, senators and other APC candidates would emerge victorious in the 2027 elections. item.title: Harvard Holds 3.04 Million Bitcoin ETF Shares Steady
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Harvard Holds 3.04 Million Bitcoin ETF Shares Steady Harvard Management Company left its stake in BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust unchanged at 3,044,612 shares in the third quarter, a position valued at $144.1 million as of Sept. 30 and now worth about $110.6 million after bitcoin’s slide. The university’s endowment manager disclosed the holding in a Form 13F filed Friday, covering the quarter ended Sept. 30. The share count is the same one Harvard reported on June 30 and on March 31. At 10:40 a.m. ET Monday, IBIT traded at $36.32, putting the stake at about $110.6 million, a paper decline of roughly $33.6 million, or 23%, from the value in the filing. The Sept. 30 close of $47.34 matches the price implied by the reported value. The same 3,044,612 shares were worth $101.4 million on June 30 and $117.0 million on March 31, so the position rose in value during the third quarter as bitcoin recovered, then gave back a large share of that gain after the quarter ended. Even after the November slide, the stake is still worth more than it was at midyear. IBIT was Harvard’s eighth-largest position among 18 holdings in a 13F portfolio valued at $3.95 billion, or about 3.6% of that publicly disclosed book of U.S. securities, which does not include the rest of the endowment. The largest holding was Space Exploration Technologies, reported at $1.29 billion. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing was second, at $616.5 million. That ranking is a sharp change from late 2025, when the bitcoin ETF was Harvard’s largest publicly disclosed position. First bought in 2025, then cut, then held Harvard first reported an IBIT position in its filing for the quarter ended June 30, 2025: 1,906,000 shares worth $116.7 million. It had not listed the fund in earlier 13Fs, including the report for March 31, 2025. By Sept. 30, 2025, Harvard had tripled the stake to 6,813,612 shares, valued at $442.9 million, making IBIT its largest public holding. The endowment trimmed that position by about 21% in the fourth quarter of 2025, to 5,353,612 shares worth $265.8 million, and opened a first stake in BlackRock’s iShares Ethereum Trust of 3,870,900 shares, valued at $86.8 million. It cut the bitcoin ETF again in the first quarter of 2026, by about 2.31 million shares, or 43%, to the 3,044,612 shares it still reported on Sept. 30, and sold the Ethereum fund entirely. The latest filing lists no other bitcoin or crypto ETFs. The remaining IBIT position is still larger, in share terms, than the 1.91 million shares Harvard first disclosed. Gold now outweighs the bitcoin ETF Harvard’s gold ETFs are now much larger than its bitcoin position. The same 13F lists 1,161,000 shares of SPDR Gold Shares worth $442.2 million, the portfolio’s third-largest holding, and 1,980,085 shares of the iShares Gold Trust worth $154.6 million. Combined, the two gold funds were valued at $596.8 million, more than four times the IBIT stake. The iShares Gold Trust share count was unchanged from June

item.title: Massive data centres collectively use as much electricity as an entire US state
item.description: Construction work on an AI data centre in Texas covering nearly 40 square kilometres, which will have a capacity of 600 megawatts Backyard Productions/Alamy The largest data centres in the US are using roughly the same amount of power collectively each year as one of the country’s major states, according to new figures that underscore the size and impact these massive facilities are having on local power grids. The rapid development of artificial intelligence systems has triggered a “fast and furious” expansion of data centres across the US, in particular of very large “hyperscale” data centres that support AI tools, cloud computing and large language models, says Francesca Dominici at Harvard University. But tracking the power consumption and carbon emissions impact of these facilities is difficult, as many data centre operators don’t publicly report such information. Advertisement Read more SpaceXAI data centre may have led to Mississippi air pollution spike Together with colleagues, Dominici spent two years pulling together information on 403 hyperscale data centres in the US to estimate their electricity consumption and associated carbon dioxide emissions. “Doing these measurements took an enormous amount of work,” she says. The team estimates that the hyperscale data centres collectively used about 82 terawatt-hours (TWh) of electricity between May 2024 and April 2025, equivalent to about 1.8 per cent of total US electricity use. This electricity use outstrips the annual power consumption of states such as Missouri, Kentucky and New Jersey. The upper bound of the team’s estimate – 99 TWh per year – would see hyperscale data centres rival the annual power consumption of states such as Indiana, Michigan and Washington. This vast power consumption has a significant climate impact. The researchers estimate that roughly 54 per cent of attributed generation was supplied by fossil fuel sources, with annual carbon dioxide emissions reaching 25.7 million tonnes – equivalent to the emissions from 67 natural gas power plants . The findings are in line with international estimates of data centre power use from the International Energy Agency and are therefore “not particularly shocking”, says Alex de Vries-Gao , a data scientist at the Free University of Amsterdam. “This just confirms the magnitude of the impacts that these facilities are having across the board.” Free newsletter Sign up to The Earth Edition Sign up to newsletter But he points out that the study relies on commercial data that is difficult to independently verify, and a set of assumptions on the power use and operating capacity of each facility. “You can’t really validate the results,” he warns. Yury Dvorkin at Johns Hopkins University in Maryland adds that the analysis is relatively “coarse”, not accounting for factors such as how network constraints impact grid power emissions. “They ignore a lot of nuance,” he says. “There are definitely a lot of assumptions baked in [to the study],”

item.title: Could there be an ancient alien satellite in Earth's orbit? How the 'Black Knight' conspiracy theory has survived for over 100 years
item.description:
Micah Hanks is a science reporter and podcaster focusing on space and astronomy, and Editor at TheDebrief.org. Follow him on X @MicahHanks.

In the final days of 1998, as astronauts aboard NASA's Space Shuttle Endeavor were working during one of the early missions to assemble the International Space Station , crew members from the STS-88 mission captured photographs of a dark colored, unusually shaped object drifting through space. Despite its unusual appearance in the photographs, the object had a conventional explanation, and one that was known to the astronauts at that time: it was one of several thermal covers that had been wrapped around trunnion pins used in the space station's construction. Upon noticing the "escape" of one of the covers, Mission Commander Bob Cabana remarked over the radio to fellow astronaut Jerry Ross that "one of the thermal covers got away from you." Seeing the cover drifting away, a frustrated Ross snapped a photograph of it. Yet despite the innocuous story behind the images, they have nonetheless helped fuel belief in an unusual Space Age conspiracy theory: one involving the alleged presence of an ancient satellite, presumably of alien origin, that has long been orbiting our planet — perhaps since the end of the last Ice Age. According to proponents of this theory, the object photographed by Ross in 1998 is actually what many call the " Black Knight Satellite ," and is only one piece of evidence they point to in a long succession of unrelated — and often misinterpreted — events in modern history that supposedly lend further evidence to the alleged alien spacecraft's existence. So how did such a legend gain traction in the first place, with some versions alleging that NASA and the U.S. government have worked to conceal evidence of the alleged space object's existence from the public? Odd detections at Colorado Springs Depending on which version of the story you come across, the strange roots of the Black Knight conspiracy theory might be traced all the way back to the nineteenth century, when the famous inventor Nikola Tesla began detecting unusual electrical signal s while conducting radio experiments at his laboratory in Colorado Springs. At the time, Tesla considered whether the signals might be communications from intelligent aliens on nearby planets, although the likely source had actually been terrestrial radio interference. Notably, Tesla also never claimed that the emissions might be coming from an object in Earth's orbit; nonetheless, some proponents of the Black Knight Satellite theories have incorporated Tesla's experiments into the mythos, suggesting they may represent some of the earliest detections of a mysterious object lurking near Earth. item.title: Has AI’s ‘Black October’ changed the way you secure your code?
item.description: October ’26 might be remembered as a seminal moment for software developers and application security teams. AI agents are investigating unfamiliar systems, testing ways to get in and adjusting their next move when an attempt fails. Anyone with a credit card can use that capability to come after your application. Coding agents and their tool integrations have introduced new entry points and surface areas that can be exploited. Pillar’s OpenCode disclosure in October showed how a malicious Model Context Protocol (MCP) server could execute commands on a developer’s Windows or WSL machine during authentication. A server-supplied URL reached a shell without tricking the model. In the same month, the discovery of the two PHP2Shell vulnerabilities, remote code execution bugs in the PHP runtime uncovered with the help of OpenAI’s models, brought new urgency to securing longstanding code across much of the internet. Microsoft revealed that an agent moved from searching GitHub for exposed credentials to stealing Azure Key Vault data in five minutes. When its cloud API requests failed, the agent corrected the API versions and tried again until they succeeded. A report by Anthropic described individual operators using agent frameworks for multi-victim campaigns that previously required specialist teams. Agents carried out reconnaissance, exploitation and data theft across targets in parallel, making sophisticated operations accessible with less hands-on work. In a recent analysis, Tomasz Tunguz estimated the model cost of a 100-million-token attack workload using GLM-5.3, a low-cost model: 100 million tokens × $0.902 per million = $90.20. That is roughly 98% to 99% below the $5,000 to $10,000 frontier-model estimate cited by Bank for International Settlements (BIS) for a comparable cyber attack. Tunguz’s figure covers model usage only, not the full cost of an attack. Even still, it shows how trivially cheap it is now for attackers to go after any codebase, with the spend falling from thousands of dollars to under $100. These new agentic attacks should make every team take another look at the code they’ve been running for years. Engineering and security teams need to find and fix weaknesses in their own applications before an attacker with an army of AI agents gets there first. Security has to become every developer’s responsibility Traditional AppSec checks such as rule-based static analysis, dependency scanning and secret detection are no longer enough on their own. Developers, engineering leaders, and security teams also need defensive AI agents that trace attack paths, uncover missing safeguards and business-logic vulnerabilities, and help fix them. Developers’ responsibility doesn’t stop at the code they’re writing now. An application already in production without known vulnerabilities might still get exploited by an AI agent looking for ways to skip a permission check or business rule. The gap only shows up when a request is traced through the codebase
